concept: Regression line of x on y
prompt:
The hours of revision, $x$, and test scores, $y$, of five students are:

| $x$ | 2 | 4 | 5 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $y$ | 52 | 60 | 63 | 72 | 78 |

A student scored 70 on the test. Use the appropriate regression line to estimate how many hours they revised, and explain your choice of line.
markscheme:
To predict $x$ from $y$, use the regression line of $x$ on $y$: $x=0.233y-9.96$ **(M1)(A1)**

$x\approx0.233(70)-9.96\approx6.4$ hours **(A1)**

The $y$-on-$x$ line minimises vertical errors and is designed for predicting $y$; rearranging it does not give the best predictor of $x$.

concept: Choosing the regression line for prediction
prompt: A scientist has the regression lines of $y$ on $x$ and of $x$ on $y$ for a data set with $r=0.6$. Which line should be used to estimate $y$ when $x$ is known, and what happens to the two lines as $r\to\pm1$?
markscheme: Use $y$ on $x$ to estimate $y$ **(A1)**. As $|r|\to1$ the two lines get closer, becoming identical when the correlation is perfect. Both always pass through $(\bar x,\bar y)$.
